task:
Design the fastest safe migration of the existing self-hosted Octopus integration from the expiring legacy Hetzner host to `ed-finder-prod`, under issue #540 and a roughly 24-hour deadline. Start from exact current origin/main `fd64ef8e14b5b026cec2d14949115ab681fb0b7d`. Read CLAUDE.md, docs/ROADMAP.md, issue #540, current `chatgpt-ops.yml` and `chatgpt-ed-new-ops.yml`, their environment/SSH boundaries and tests, current nginx/Compose Octopus integration, and official Octopus v1.0.122 self-hosting/App Manifest/provider docs. Also account for active preparation worker run 33444386146, but do not modify or assume its unreviewed output. Investigation only: do not modify files, commit, push, deploy, access either host, use secrets, connect to databases, modify DNS/GitHub Apps/firewalls, start or stop containers, or expose any credential.

The owner has authorised reusing the existing external integration credentials because the old host expires soon: existing GitHub App ID/private key/client credentials/webhook secret/slug, Anthropic and OpenAI API keys, and existing Octopus UI basic-auth credential where practical. Fresh installation-local secrets (new Octopus PostgreSQL password, BETTER_AUTH_SECRET, OCTOPUS_DATA_KEY and temporary admin password) should still be generated on the new host.

Produce a concrete implementation design for an audited one-time dual-host transfer and cutover using the repository's two separate GitHub environments (`hetzner-operator` for the old host and `ed-new-operator` for the new host). The design must never expose plaintext secrets to GitHub logs, issue text, source control, workflow inputs/outputs, artifacts, process argv, or environment variables beyond the minimum trusted process. Prefer a three-job hybrid-encryption protocol: new host creates an ephemeral recipient key whose public material can cross jobs; old-host job streams the legacy `/opt/octopus/.env` or an allowlisted export directly into authenticated encryption; only ciphertext is retained briefly as a GitHub artifact; new-host job decrypts locally and imports only an explicit allowlist while preserving newly generated local secrets. Verify whether OpenSSL CMS, age, or another already-available pinned mechanism is the safest practical choice, including authenticity/integrity, arbitrary-size payload support, cleanup, crash recovery and artifact-retention/deletion limitations. Do not recommend home-grown crypto.

Specify a robust dotenv transfer/import contract that handles the existing GitHub App PEM representation without sourcing arbitrary shell code. Define the allowlist and distinguish external reusable values from local values that must not be copied. Include at minimum OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, GITHUB_APP_ID, GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY, GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET, GITHUB_APP_CLIENT_ID, GITHUB_APP_CLIENT_SECRET, NEXT_PUBLIC_GITHUB_APP_SLUG, GITHUB_STATE_SECRET, and the basic-auth file if it is separate. Verify likely actual Octopus variable names against v1.0.122; note optional keys that should be copied only when present. Plaintext temporary files on either runner should be avoided; if unavoidable on a host, require root-only tmpfs/mode 0600, atomic use and guaranteed cleanup.

Design the exact no-duplicate cutover order. The new Octopus web/DB/Qdrant may be started privately with `ENABLE_REVIEW_WORKERS=false` and no active public webhook; migrate, health/version/restart-test and configure it; then quiesce the old worker/webhook path, transfer/reuse app credentials, switch the existing `octopus.ed-finder.app` route and GitHub webhook target, enable one new review worker, and prove a single exact-head review. Explain whether the existing GitHub App webhook URL can simply continue using the same hostname while DNS/public edge changes underneath it, and what must be changed if DNS already points to the new V3 public edge versus the old host. Provide rollback commands/state for every mutating phase.

Account for the circular reviewer outage: the migration/restoration PR cannot receive a working Octopus review until the migration succeeds. Define the narrow one-time owner waiver evidence required, while keeping exact-head CI, Codex, manual security review and no unresolved findings mandatory.

End with: (1) recommended transfer mechanism and why; (2) exact reusable-secret allowlist and excluded local secrets; (3) workflow/job topology and environment boundaries; (4) implementation files/tests required; (5) minute-by-minute or phase-by-phase cutover order within the deadline; (6) rollback plan; (7) exact points where owner input is unavoidable; and (8) hard blockers or assumptions to verify before any write. No implementation in this run.
